title: The vyx economy on a longer sample: T = 860 and a 720-month window, the same 125 evaluation months
question: Is DKKM's shortfall from its population ceiling in vyx a data limit?
notes:
X3 (docs/RESULTS.md, KP14 proposals). The vyx ECONOMY unchanged -- same parameters, same G and integ solves -- simulated for 860 months instead of 500 and estimated on a 720-month window instead of 360, so the evaluation months are the same count (845 - 720 = 125). The ridge grid gains 1e-4 below vyx's smallest penalty, which won in 9 of 10 vyx seeds.

WHY: in vyx the linear methods reach 99% of their population ceiling and DKKM 74% of its, and DKKM wants less shrinkage than the grid allows. If DKKM's shortfall is data, doubling the window closes part of it and leaves the linear methods where they are.

PREDICTION (2026-09-13): DKKM +0.03 to +0.08 over vyx's 0.7475; the linear methods within +0.01 of vyx's 0.6428; gap +0.13 to +0.17; room unchanged within seed noise, since the economy is the same and the oracle ceilings move only with the month sample. FALSIFIED IF DKKM gains less than +0.02. Report the gap restricted to vyx's grid (kappa >= 0.001) beside the full-grid gap, so the window and the grid extension are separable.

OWN TAG: result files are named by model, tag and seed only, so under tag vyx this run would overwrite vyx's panels, moments and oracle files.

REUSED SOLVES: pins vyx's G f7be27e39d2b530f and integ 84e195172f091cd2, recorded for var-kp_vy-vyx-v2; this spec causes no solve of its own. estimation.fair_linear: the linear methods are also scored with the EW market unpenalised (finding 8); `lin` keeps its definition over ff, fm, linrank, linlev. Memory: vyx's oracle peaked at 30.6 GiB at T=500; expect ~53 GiB.

changes: estimation window 360 -> 720 (125 evaluation months either way)
tag vyxT860; solves reused from var-kp_vy-vyx-v2
lineage.retired: RETIRED 2026-09-15 with the measurement protocol (variants/common/protocol.py). This spec's ECONOMY is var-kp_vy-vyx-v2's, parameter for parameter and solve for solve: it differed only in T (860 vs 500), the estimation window (720 vs 360) and a ridge grid extended to 1e-4. Those are numerical choices, so this was never another economy -- it was vyx measured differently, and reporting it beside vyx made a sample length look like an economic finding. Its results are deleted rather than archived and quoted. The question it asked, whether DKKM's shortfall from its ceiling is data, is now asked on protocol: the wide ridge grid every economy shares removes the censoring that reading rested on. Nothing supersedes this spec, because nothing replaces it.

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the pre-2026-09-07 single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the old fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
